Proof 1.1–4.1: compact evaluation maxima give a strictly positive uniform margin, including empty K separately. A nonnegative small-support convolution square has positive f(0), an integrable nonnegative transform and exact pointwise inversion. Tail mass <f(0)/8 and ε||hat f||1<f(0)/4 give |f(x)−f(0)|<f(0)/2, hence nonvanishing and membership in U. Translation gives the basis and compact-open evaluation gives both topology directions. F4 now explicitly constructs the cutoff support; step 3.1 shrinks a potentially nonopen neighbourhood before invoking step 2.1. The changed positivity wording is sound polish (g≥0 already makes the convolution real nonnegative), not a new defect. Trivial G and empty compact sets work. Koerner Lemma 13.1, p. 26 agrees. Proof 1.1–5.1: q·conjugate(hat f) is integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz; compact-density measures are regular by the explicit F5 construction and L1/total-variation limits preserve regularity. Orthogonality to every translated f makes its inverse transform zero with the correct conjugate phase, so independently read Fourier–Stieltjes uniqueness gives q·conjugate(hat f)=0 a.e. Local indicator transforms are nonzero near each dual character. The sigma-compact essential support of this particular q reduces its open cover to countably many finite covers, avoiding uncountable unions of null sets and any global sigma-finiteness assumption. Isometry/completeness gives a closed range and the exact AC Hilbert-complement lemma gives surjectivity. The zero class/trivial group are covered. Loomis 36D, pp. 145–146 and Einsiedler–Ward p. 435 confirm the conclusion; the current local uniqueness route is independently read and precedes biduality. Source changes only. Counterexample 1.1–4.1: algebraic Hom(Z,T) identifies with T. The coordinate functional from an arbitrary Hamel basis is normalized by its nonzero coefficient in 1, giving Q-linear T with T(1)=1 and killing another basis vector; no unsupported assumption that the basis contains 1 is made. T preserves Z and descends to R/Z. If its induced map were a power k, T−kI would map into Z; divisibility forces every value into the intersection of nZ, hence zero, contrary to the basis values. It is continuous on the discrete X and outside the evaluation image. The compact-open comparison is justified by finite compact subsets of Z and evaluation at 1; AC implies DC before general biduality. The Hamel supplier proof and real-character classification were read. Loomis 35D–35F supplies only the comparison; the witness is locally constructed.
